mainTopic: Acquiring a lost item for someone else, and acquiring through a person's four אמות
overview: This amud finishes the argument between רב נחמן and עולא over whether picking up a lost item for someone else gets it for him. עולא explains the rider משנה as a case where the finder said he took it for himself from the start, and the two argue over the extra word תחילה. Next, רב נחמן and רב חסדא rule that lifting a מציאה for a friend does not acquire it, because it takes the item away from everyone else. רבא challenges this from a hired worker. רב נחמן answers that a worker's hand is like the boss's hand, even though a worker may quit, since Jews are servants of ה׳. רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the friend does acquire. A new משנה teaches that falling on a מציאה does not acquire it. ריש לקיש says a person's four אמות acquire for him, and the גמרא defends this against a challenge from the משנה in פאה: by falling, the poor person showed he did not want to acquire through his four אמות.

steps.title: The rider משנה fits only רב נחמן's view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן argues that the משנה fits the רבנן on his view. On עולא's view it fits neither the רבנן nor רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is our משנה? It is the רבנן. But if you say the dispute is only about a rich person picking up for a poor person, and that when a poor person picks up for a poor person everyone agrees the other one gets it, then whose view is this משנה? It is neither the רבנן nor רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his challenge to עולא. Our משנה works well with his own view but seems to fit nobody on עולא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן holds that the רבנן say picking up for another never gets it for him, so the משנה (where the finder keeps it) is the רבנן. עולא holds that the argument is only about a rich person picking up פאה for a poor person. A finder could have kept the item himself, just like a poor person can take פאה for himself, so on עולא's view everyone should agree the rider gets it. That makes the משנה fit no one.

keyTerms.meaning: A rich person and a poor person (the פאה case)

steps.confusionAlert: The speaker here is רב נחמן challenging עולא, not the other way around. The answer in the next step is עולא's.

phrases.english: Our משנה, whose view is it? It is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the end of רב נחמן's 'it works for me' half. On his view the רבנן say grabbing for someone else doesn't get it for him.

phrases.english: But if you say
that the dispute is about a rich person and a poor person,
phrases.notes: This is the פאה case: a rich person gathers פאה for a poor person.

phrases.english: but when a poor person gathers for a poor person
everyone agrees he acquired it for him,
then whose view is this?
Neither the Rabbis nor Rabbi Eliezer!
phrases.notes: A finder could have kept it himself, just like a poor person. So on עולא's view everyone should give it to the rider.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא אי אמרת בעשיר ועני מחלוקת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that רב נחמן started before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's claim that a poor person gathering for a poor person acquires it for him according to everyone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A finder is like a poor person, since he could acquire the item himself. On עולא's view the rider should get it, yet the משנה gives it to the finder.

steps.title: The finder said he took it for himself from the start
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the משנה is a case where the finder said he picked it up for himself from the very beginning.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our משנה is where he said 'from the start.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers רב נחמן. He limits the משנה to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא agrees that normally the rider would get the item. In the משנה, though, the finder declared that he meant to take it for himself from the moment he lifted it. Because of that, he never picked it up for the rider at all, so the משנה does not contradict עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, at the outset

phrases.english: He said to him:
Our משנה is where he said 'from the start.'
phrases.notes: The finder said: 'I picked it up for myself from the very start, never for you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה מתניתין דאמר תחילה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a narrow case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה gives the item to the finder even though he picked it up for the rider
steps.terutzMaskana: The finder declared that he lifted it for himself from the outset, so he never acquired it for the rider

steps.title: The word תחילה in the סיפא supports עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports עולא. It points out that the word תחילה in the סיפא is unnecessary unless it is there to teach that the רישא also involves תחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So too it makes sense, because the last part teaches: If, after he gave it to him, he said 'I acquired it first,' he said nothing. Why do I need 'first' in the last part? It is obvious that even if he didn't say 'first,' he meant 'first.' Rather, isn't it teaching us this: the first part is where he said 'first'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for עולא's answer from the wording of the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the סיפא, the finder already handed the item over and only then claimed he took it first. Any claim made at that point must be about the time before he gave it, so writing תחילה there adds nothing. The extra word must be a hint that the רישא is also a case where he said תחילה, just as עולא said.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it makes sense (support follows)
The last part of the משנה
He said nothing; his words don't count
The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
for the last part teaches:
If, after he gave it to him,
he said, 'I acquired it first' –
he has said nothing.
phrases.notes: Once he handed it over, the rider keeps it.

phrases.english: Why do I need 'first' in the last part?

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא, אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אָמַר תְּחִילָּה,
phrases.english: It's obvious, even if he didn't say 'first,'
he means 'first.'
phrases.notes: He already gave it away, so any claim he makes now has to be about before he gave it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it teaching us this:
the first part is where he said 'first.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הכי נמי מסתברא דקתני סיפא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports עולא's answer from step 2
steps.raayaObject: עולא's reading that the רישא is a case where he said תחילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The extra word תחילה in the סיפא of the משנה

steps.title: רב נחמן: the סיפא sheds light on the רישא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains the word תחילה in the סיפא differently. It shows by contrast that the רישא is a case where he did NOT say תחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one: The last part was taught to reveal the first part. The last part is where he said 'first'; the first part is where he did not say 'first.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב נחמן's reply, which pushes away the proof from step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the word תחילה in the סיפא is a deliberate contrast. Since the סיפא makes a point of mentioning it, the רישא must be a case without it, and the finder still keeps the item. That fits רב נחמן's view that picking up for someone else does not get it for him until it is handed over.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other sage)
To reveal, to shed light on

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: the משנה is a case where the finder said 'I took it for myself from the start.' רב נחמן: the finder keeps it even without saying so, and the word תחילה in the סיפא is only there to contrast with the רישא.

phrases.english: And the other one:
He taught the last part to shed light on the first part.
The last part is where he said 'first';
the first part is where he did not say 'first.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ואידך תנא סיפא לגלויי רישא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support brought in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the word תחילה, but not עולא's position itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The extra word can be read as a contrast: the סיפא says תחילה to show that the רישא does not

steps.title: Lifting a found item for someone else does not acquire it for him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב חסדא both rule that if a person lifts a מציאה on behalf of a friend, the friend does not acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רב חסדא both say: if someone lifts a found item for his friend, the friend does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling. Picking up a lost item for someone else does not make it belong to that other person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally lifting (הגבהה) is how you acquire an ownerless item. This ruling says the lifting works only for yourself. It cannot transfer ownership to someone else. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lifts (an item), the act that acquires it
For his friend, on behalf of another person
Did not acquire, does not become the owner

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman and Rav Ḥisda
who both say:
one who lifts a found item for his friend –
his friend does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַב חִסְדָּא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new unit that states רב נחמן's own position, together with רב חסדא. It is the position he defended against עולא in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifting a מציאה on behalf of another person does not acquire it for that person.

steps.title: The reason: grabbing for one person at the expense of others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ruling by comparing it to someone who seizes a debtor's property for one creditor when this hurts other creditors. Such a seizure does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? This is like someone who grabs property for a creditor in a way that causes a loss to others. Someone who grabs for a creditor in a way that causes a loss to others does not acquire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the friend does not acquire the item. It answers with a known rule about creditors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A creditor may grab a debtor's property himself. An outsider may not grab it for him if that pushes out the other creditors. Here too, everyone has an equal right to an ownerless item. So lifting it for your friend takes that chance away from everyone else, and it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: One who seizes or grabs property
A creditor, someone who is owed money

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the friend is a creditor here. The case of the creditor is only a comparison. Just as you cannot grab for one creditor at the other creditors' expense, you cannot lift a found item for one person at everyone else's expense.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is like one who seizes for a creditor
in a situation where he causes a loss to others,
phrases.notes: The "others" are the other creditors, who would lose out if one creditor got paid first.

phrases.english: and one who seizes for a creditor
in a situation where he causes a loss to others –
does not acquire.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the ruling of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does lifting for a friend fail to acquire for the friend?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is like seizing for a creditor when this hurts others, and such seizing does not acquire.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the case of a hired worker who finds something
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא. A worker keeps what he finds if he was hired for a specific job. If he was hired for general work, what he finds belongs to the boss. This seems to show a person can acquire a found item for someone else, against רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: a worker's found item belongs to himself. When is this said? When the boss told him, "Weed with me today" or "Hoe with me today." But if he told him, "Do work with me today," the found item belongs to the boss!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's ruling with a ברייתא about a hired worker.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the general-work case, the worker lifts the item and the boss becomes the owner. That looks exactly like lifting a found item for someone else and having it work. So the ברייתא seems to contradict רב נחמן's rule that the friend does not acquire.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to explain how a worker's found item can belong to the boss without breaking רב נחמן's rule. That is the next stage of the סוגיא.

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection to Rav Naḥman:
The found item of a worker belongs to himself.
When is this said?
When the employer said to him:
"Weed with me today,"
or "Hoe with me today."
But if he said to him:
"Do work with me today" –
his found item belongs to the employer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 5 and its reason in step 6, using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's rule that lifting a found item for another does not acquire it for him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, a worker hired for general work lifts a found item and the boss acquires it. That shows lifting for another person does work, against רב נחמן.

steps.title: A worker is different: his hand is the boss's hand
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא: a hired worker is a special case, because his hand counts as the employer's own hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבא: A worker is different, because his hand is like the hand of the employer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's challenge from the ברייתא about the worker. He says a hired worker is a special case and proves nothing about ordinary people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person lifts a מציאה for a friend, he hurts other people who could have grabbed it, so it does not work. A worker is different, because the boss already 'owns' his working hand. So when the worker picks something up, it is as if the boss himself picked it up.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used to show a case is special and cannot be used as a proof.
His hand is like the employer's hand

phrases.english: He said to him: A worker is different,
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן answering רבא's question from the step before.

phrases.english: for his hand is like the hand of the employer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שָׁאנֵי פּוֹעֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's קשיא from the ברייתא of the worker in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (אוקימתא of a special status)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worker's finds going to the boss show that anyone can acquire a מציאה for someone else.
steps.terutzMaskana: A worker's hand is treated as the boss's own hand, so this is not acquiring for another person at all.

steps.title: But a worker can quit in the middle of the day
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the idea that a worker's hand belongs to the boss, quoting רב that a worker may quit even at midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say that a worker may back out of his job even in the middle of the day?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's answer. If a worker can walk off the job whenever he wants, how can his hand really belong to the boss?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's answer needs a strong bond between worker and boss. רב's rule that a worker can quit at any time suggests the bond is weak and built in the worker's favor. If so, the worker's hand should not count as the boss's hand.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [he] say? This introduces a challenge from another ruling.
To back out or change one's mind
In the middle of the day

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
phrases.notes: רבא is the one asking here, still pushing against רב נחמן.

phrases.english: A worker can back out
even in the middle of the day!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that a worker's hand is like the employer's hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A worker can quit at any time, so he is not truly bound to the boss. That makes it hard to say his hand belongs to the boss.

steps.title: Quitting has a separate reason: servants of ה׳, not servants to servants
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן explains that while the worker is working, his hand is the boss's hand. His right to quit comes from a separate פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבא: As long as he has not backed out, his hand is like the employer's hand. When he does back out, that is for a different reason, as it is written: 'For the children of Israel are servants to Me, they are My servants.' This means they are not servants to servants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his answer. He separates two things: while the worker is on the job, and the worker's right to quit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The right to quit does not show that the worker-boss bond is weak. It comes from a special rule of the תורה: a Jew belongs to ה׳ and cannot be locked into serving another person. So as long as the worker stays on the job, his hand still counts fully as the boss's hand.

keyTerms.meaning: As long as he has not backed out
They are My servants, and not servants to servants

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב נחמן, a hired worker's hand is the boss's hand while he works. His right to quit comes only from the rule that Jews are servants of ה׳, not of other people.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the classic source for a worker's right to quit at any time.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: As long as he has not backed out,
he is like the hand of the employer.
When he does back out,
it is for a different reason,
as it is written: "For to Me the children of Israel are servants,
they are My servants"
and not servants to servants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כֹּל כַּמָּה דְּלָא הָדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's קשיא in step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating two different rules (a different reason)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a worker can quit, his bond to the boss must be weak.
steps.terutzMaskana: The right to quit comes from a separate פסוק. While the worker is still working, his hand is fully the boss's hand.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the friend does acquire
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: if someone lifts a מציאה for his friend, the friend acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone lifts a found object for his friend, his friend acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion, the opposite of רב נחמן and רב חסדא. רבי יוחנן says lifting a מציאה for a friend does work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן and רב חסדא said the friend does not acquire, because that would hurt others who could have taken the item. רבי יוחנן disagrees completely and says the friend acquires.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lifts. Lifting is a way of acquiring an item.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who lifts a found object for his friend:
his friend acquires it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to the ruling of רב נחמן and רב חסדא in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lifting a מציאה on behalf of a friend gives the friend ownership.

steps.title: Our משנה is a case of 'give it to me'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains why our משנה does not contradict him: there, the rider said 'give it to me,' not 'acquire it for me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say our משנה shows otherwise, it is a case where he said 'Give it to me' and did not say 'Acquire it for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן deals ahead of time with a question someone might ask from our משנה. In the משנה the rider did not acquire the item, but that is because of how he worded his request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the rider asked the walker to hand him the item, and the walker kept it for himself. רבי יוחנן says the rider only asked to be handed the item, so he would own it only once it reached him. If the rider had said 'acquire it for me,' the walker's lifting would have made it the rider's right away.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. This brings up a possible objection.

steps.confusionAlert: The rule did not change between the two cases. Only the wording did. 'Give it to me' means 'hand it over,' while 'acquire it for me' asks the walker to take ownership for him right now.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says lifting for a friend works. The משנה is no problem, because there the rider only said 'give it to me.'

phrases.english: And if you say: our Mishnah [shows otherwise],
phrases.notes: This is our משנה about the rider and the walker, where the walker keeps the item even though the rider asked for it.

phrases.english: it is where he said "Give it to me,"
and did not say "Acquire it for me."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 11 against a possible question from the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the rider in the משנה did not acquire, it seems lifting for another person does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rider only said 'give it to me.' Had he said 'acquire it for me,' he would have acquired through the walker's lifting.

steps.title: New משנה: falling on a found object does not acquire it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who falls on a מציאה does not acquire it. Another person who picks it up does acquire it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone saw a found object and fell on it, and another person came and took hold of it, the one who took hold of it gets it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches that just falling on a lost object is not enough to own it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Falling on the object is not one of the proper ways to acquire something. The one who actually takes hold of it, called הגבהה or החזקה, uses a real way of acquiring. So the second person wins.

keyTerms.meaning: He fell on it, as a way of claiming it

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one saw a found object and fell upon it,
and another came and took hold of it,
the one who took hold of it acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רָאָה אֶת הַמְּצִיאָה וְנָפַל עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It starts a new topic after the discussion of acquiring for someone else.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Falling on a מציאה does not acquire it. The one who takes hold of it acquires it.

steps.title: A person's four אמות acquire for him everywhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, quoting אבא כהן ברדלא, says the space of four אמות around a person acquires ownerless items for him anywhere. The רבנן made this rule to prevent fights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said in the name of אבא כהן ברדלא: a person's four אמות acquire things for him in every place. What is the reason? The רבנן set this up so that people would not come to fight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule: the area right around a person, four אמות, works like his own property to acquire things. The rule was made to stop people from fighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you must pick up or take hold of an object to acquire it. This rule says that once an ownerless item is within four אמות of you, it is yours. The rule is a rabbinic enactment, a תקנה, made because people would otherwise fight over the item.

keyTerms.meaning: The space of four cubits around a person
In every place, not only in his own property

steps.confusionAlert: This rule does not come from the תורה. The רבנן made it to keep the peace. That is why the גמרא asks for its reason.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא כֹּהֵן בַּרְדְּלָא:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Abba Kohen Bardela:
The four cubits of a person
acquire for him in every place.
What is the reason? The Rabbis enacted it,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are part of the corrected wording; some versions don't have them.

phrases.english: so that people would not come to quarrel.
phrases.notes: The regular printed גמרא has אתי (in round brackets), and the corrected wording says ליתו. Both mean 'come'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא כֹּהֵן בַּרְדְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה about falling on a מציאה, the גמרא brings a related rule about acquiring through the space around a person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's four אמות acquire ownerless items for him anywhere. This is a rabbinic rule made to prevent fights.

steps.title: Two objections are announced, from פאה and from נזיקין
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי חייא בר יוסף challenged the rule from מסכת פאה. רבא says רבי יעקב בר אידי challenged it from נזיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: רבי חייא בר יוסף raises an objection from פאה. רבא said: רבי יעקב בר אידי raises an objection from נזיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up what comes next. The גמרא tells us two objections to רבי שמעון בן לקיש are coming, and names who raised each one. It has not explained them yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two אמוראים report different challenges, each from a different part of the משנה. The גמרא will now go through them one at a time, starting with the one from פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor, and the מסכת about it
The order or section of the משנה dealing with damages

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מוֹתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף פֵּיאָה.
phrases.english: Abaye said: Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef raises an objection from Pe'ah.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מוֹתֵיב רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידִי נְזִיקִין.
phrases.english: Rava said: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Idi raises an objection from Nezikin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מוֹתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף פֵּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It announces that the rule from step 14 will be challenged from two sources.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule that a person's four אמות acquire for him everywhere
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only announced here. The details come in the next steps.

steps.title: The משנה in פאה: falling on פאה does not acquire it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in פאה. A poor person who throws some פאה on the rest, falls on it, or spreads his cloak over it does not acquire it, and others may remove him. The same applies to a forgotten sheaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a poor person took some of the פאה and threw it on the rest, he gets nothing from it. If he fell on it or spread his cloak over it, people may move him off it. The same is true for a forgotten sheaf, עומר שכחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source behind רבי חייא בר יוסף's objection. This is setup: the actual attack on רבי שמעון בן לקיש comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in פאה says that covering or falling on the poor person's portion is not a valid way to acquire it. Other poor people may push him away and take it. The key point is that the item is right next to him, within his four אמות, and still he does not get it.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheaf forgotten in the field, which belongs to the poor

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, מוֹתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף פֵּיאָה:
phrases.english: Abaye said: Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef raises an objection from Pe'ah:

phrases.aramaic: נָטַל מִקְצָת פֵּיאָה וְזָרַק עַל הַשְּׁאָר –
phrases.english: If he took some of the pe'ah and threw it on the rest,
phrases.notes: פאה 4:3. He is trying to claim the whole pile by covering it.

phrases.english: he has nothing of it.
If he fell upon it,
or spread his cloak over it,
they remove him from it.
And the same is true of a forgotten sheaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, מוֹתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף פֵּיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא repeats אביי's opening line from step 15, now to actually quote the משנה in פאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing some פאה on the rest, falling on it, or covering it with a cloak does not acquire it. The same is true for עומר שכחה.

steps.title: Why didn't his four אמות acquire the פאה for him?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף argues that if four אמות acquire everywhere, the poor person's four אמות should have acquired the פאה for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a person's four אמות acquire for him everywhere, then let his own four אמות acquire the פאה for him!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the objection is stated directly. The case in פאה seems to contradict רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor person is lying right on the פאה, so it is surely within his four אמות. If four אמות acquire anywhere, he should own it. Yet the משנה says others may push him off. That seems to show four אמות do not acquire.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule that ארבע אמות acquire is now under attack. A poor person lying on פאה, well within his four אמות, still does not acquire it.

phrases.english: And if you say

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל אָדָם קוֹנוֹת לוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: that a person's four cubits acquire for him everywhere,
let his own four cubits acquire it for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל אָדָם קוֹנוֹת לוֹ בְּכׇל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It uses the משנה quoted in step 16 to attack the rule from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן לקיש's rule that a person's four אמות acquire for him everywhere
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The poor person's body is on the פאה, so it is within his four אמות. Yet the משנה says he does not acquire it. That contradicts the rule.

steps.title: The poor person did not say 'I will acquire'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה in פאה is talking about a poor person who never said he wanted to acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with a case where he did not say: 'I will acquire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבי חייא בר יוסף's challenge. It limits the משנה in פאה to a case where the poor person never said 'I will acquire.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was that the poor person's ארבע אמות should have acquired the פאה for him. The answer is that the משנה is about a specific case: he never said out loud that he wanted to acquire. So the משנה does not contradict the rule of ארבע אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? This phrase introduces a narrower case.

phrases.english: Here, with what are we dealing?
Where he did not say: 'I will acquire.'
phrases.notes: 'He' is the poor person from the משנה in פאה who fell on the produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of רבי חייא בר יוסף from Step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in פאה seemed to say that ארבע אמות never acquire for a poor person, which would contradict ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about a poor person who did not say 'I will acquire.'

steps.title: If the רבנן made the rule, why do words matter?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: the רבנן's rule of ארבע אמות should work even if the person said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the רבנן made this rule, what difference does it make that he did not say it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave. If the רבנן set up ארבע אמות to acquire automatically, saying 'I will acquire' should not be needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of ארבע אמות was made by the רבנן to prevent fights, and it does its job on its own. Normally a person does not have to say anything for it to work. So 'he did not say I will acquire' does not seem like a good reason for him to lose the פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן made a rule (a תקנה)
What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: But if the Sages instituted [this rule],
phrases.notes: He means the rule from Step 14, that a person's four אמות acquire for him.

phrases.english: when he did not say [it], what of it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי תַּקּוּן רַבָּנַן, כִּי לָא אֲמַר מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the poor person did not acquire because he did not say 'I will acquire.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן's rule of ארבע אמות works automatically, so saying something should not be required.

steps.title: By falling, he showed he did not want to acquire through ארבע אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that falling on the פאה showed the poor person wanted to acquire only by falling. That does not work, so he acquires nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he fell on it, he showed that he wanted to acquire by falling. He did not want to acquire through his ארבע אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends its answer. The poor person's own action of falling on the produce showed which way he wanted to acquire it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually ארבע אמות acquire without words. Here, though, the poor person picked a different method: falling on the produce. That told us he did not want to use his ארבע אמות. Falling is not a valid way to acquire, so he ends up with nothing, and others may take the פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is acceptable to him; he wants it
The four-cubit space around a person

steps.whatToRemember: The rule of ארבע אמות does not need words to work. But if a person shows by his actions that he wants to acquire some other way, he gives up his ארבע אמות. Then, if his chosen way does not work, he gets nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: Saying 'I will acquire' is not a requirement for ארבע אמות. Falling is what shows he chose a different method. Saying 'I will acquire' would have shown he wanted to acquire in any way that works.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer shows that a person's own choice of method can cancel the automatic rule of ארבע אמות. The second objection, from נזיקין (announced in step 15), still has to be dealt with.

phrases.english: Since he fell [on it],
he revealed his intention
that he is satisfied to acquire by falling,

phrases.aramaic: בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת לָא נִיחָא לֵיהּ דְּנִקְנֵי.
phrases.english: [but] he is not satisfied to acquire through four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דִּנְפַל, גַּלִּי דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 and supports the answer of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the person's intention through his action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ארבע אמות acquire automatically, not saying 'I will acquire' should not matter.
steps.terutzMaskana: By falling, he showed he gave up acquiring through ארבע אמות. Falling does not acquire, so he gets nothing.
